findings:
F1 — the diff publishes a new behavioural claim that nothing executes, under the very rule the round invoked to close obj-3.

Where: /home/user/fleet/indexeddb/src/browser/types.ts:268-270 (`@throws An {@link IndexedDBError} of code UNKNOWN when the cursor's source is an object store: the native call raises InvalidAccessError`) and /home/user/fleet/indexeddb/guides/indexeddb.md:296 (`a store cursor from db.store(name).cursor() throws InvalidAccessError ... so it reaches the caller as an IndexedDBError of code UNKNOWN`).

What is wrong: no test drives `seek` on a store cursor. A sweep of `seek` across /home/user/fleet/indexeddb/tests/**/*.test.ts returns only the index-cursor case at tests/src/browser/IndexedDBCursor.test.ts:81-99, the corrected fence transcription at tests/src/browser/integration.test.ts:158, and the presence guard at tests/guides.test.ts:233. A sweep of `InvalidAccessError` returns only the two prose sites. The UNKNOWN code is derived from the specification, never run.

Why it matters: `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Parity — the rule obj-4 itself cites — requires an executed assertion wherever a prose claim about behaviour sits under no fence, and states that prose rulings survive because nothing tries. This round's premise (obj-3) is that an unexecuted guide claim is a defect reaching every consumer who installs the package; this diff adds a fresh one to the same guide and to published TSDoc. If Chromium raises a different name — InvalidStateError maps to INVALID through src/browser/constants.ts, not to UNKNOWN — the published contract is wrong and no gate can see it.

What right looks like: add a case to tests/src/browser/IndexedDBCursor.test.ts beside the existing `seek` case that opens a store cursor through db.store('users').cursor(), calls `await cursor.seek(key, primary)`, and asserts the rejection is an IndexedDBError whose errorCode is 'UNKNOWN'. Where the executed code differs from UNKNOWN, correct src/browser/types.ts:268-270 and guides/indexeddb.md:296 to what the run reports rather than weakening the test.
